content.title: Miniature Assembly Progression | Local Locks, Whole Checks, Integrated Proof
content.summary: A rescue beacon progresses from support legs to one tested signal pulse. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One work surface and hand pair remain continuous. + Load-bearing components assemble before upper parts. + Every connection is visibly aligned and pressed. + A whole-object check follows each major stage. + The finished object performs one integrated proof action.
quick_start.recommended_input: Show two adult craft hands assembling an original palm-sized orange-and-slate rescue beacon on one cork work mat. Lock both legs to the housing and return to one whole-object stability check. Set the complete beacon upright, press one test button and hold the stable amber pulse.
required_anchors: One work surface and hand pair remain continuous.
Load-bearing components assemble before upper parts.
A whole-object check follows each major stage.
The finished object performs one integrated proof action.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A rescue beacon progresses from support legs to one tested signal pulse. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
